gp.text: In 2020, approximately 80% of Aerex’s revenue, and 89% of Aerex’s gross profit were generated from sales to one customer. While Aerex sells various products to this customer, Aerex’s revenue from this customer had historically been derived primarily from one specialized product. In October 2020, this customer informed Aerex that, for inventory management purposes, it was suspending its purchases of the specialized product from Aerex following 2020 for a period of approximately one year. This customer informed Aerex at that time that it expected to recommence its purchases of the specialized product from Aerex beginning with the first quarter of 2022. As a result of this anticipated loss of revenue for Aerex, we updated our projections for our manufacturing reporting unit’s future cash flows. Such projections assumed, in part, that Aerex’s major customer would recommence its purchases from Aerex in 2022 but at a reduced aggregate amount, as compared to 2020. Based upon these updated projections, we tested our manufacturing reporting unit’s goodwill for possible impairment as of December 31, 2020 using the discounted cash flow and guideline public company methods, with a weighting of 80% and 20% applied to these two methods, respectively.

We paid approximately $2.3 million for dividends in October 2026. Our liquidity requirements may also include future quarterly dividends, if such dividends are declared by our Board.

Bulk revenue.text: Gross profit dollars for our bulk segment increased to $3,378,980 (33% of bulk revenue) for 2026 as compared to $2,910,001 (35% of bulk revenue) due to the increased revenue. The reduction in bulk segment gross profit as a percentage of revenue from 2025 to 2026 reflects higher diesel costs and incremental maintenance expenses.

Services revenue.text: Gross profit for the services segment decreased to $1,321,583 (14% of services revenue) in 2026 from $3,844,421 (27% of services revenue) in 2025 due to the revenue decrease and a lower average gross profit percentage generated under our contracts.

Retail revenue.text: Retail segment gross profit decreased to $4,184,146 (51% of retail revenue) for 2026 as compared to $4,323,082 (56% of retail revenue) for 2025 due to the lower rates that became effective August 1, 2026 under the new retail license.

Manufacturing revenue.text: Manufacturing revenue decreased to $2,811,843 for 2026, as compared to $4,664,433 for 2025. The decrease in manufacturing revenue for 2026 resulted from a decrease in the total dollar amount of contracts completed and in progress. We believe, based on current projections, that manufacturing revenue for the full 2026 fiscal year will be less than the manufacturing revenue generated for the 2025 fiscal year.

intro.text: Consolidated Water Co. Ltd. develops and operates advanced water treatment plants and water distribution systems. The company designs, constructs and operates seawater desalination facilities in the Cayman Islands, The Bahamas and the British Virgin Islands, and designs, constructs and operates water treatment and reuse facilities in the United States. ​ The company also manufactures and services a wide range of products and provides design, engineering, management, operating and other services applicable to commercial and municipal water production, supply and treatment, and industrial water and wastewater treatment.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For fiscal year 2025, our retail water, bulk water, services and manufacturing segments generated approximately 26%, 25%, 35% and 14%, respectively, of our consolidated revenue.
For fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023, our retail water operations accounted for approximately 26%, 24%, and 17%, respectively, of our consolidated revenue.
The provision for credit losses for our retail operations has historically represented less than 1% of our total annual retail sales.
